summary: @onereach/orest-vue-demi-vue2 preinstall drops Bun runtime and executes obfuscated payload
details: Package advertises itself as a trivial vue-demi re-export shim (dist/index.mjs is ~4KB of globalThis['VueDemi'] proxy exports), but its package.json declares a preinstall hook (`node setup.mjs`) that downloads a Bun runtime archive from github.com/oven-sh/bun releases into a temporary directory, extracts it, chmods the binary to 0o755, and invokes it via execFileSync to run a bundled sibling file math_init.js. math_init.js is a single ~728KB line prefixed `// @bun @bun-cjs`, obfuscated with a string-array shuffle routine (WV8StW pushes/shifts a large numeric/string literal array) and hex-named identifiers. The payload executes under a freshly downloaded alternate JS runtime at npm install time, sidestepping inspection of what the bundle actually does. A vue-demi shim has no functional need for an alternate runtime or a 728KB opaque bundle; the shim exports are a cover for install-time execution of attacker-controlled code. The `@onereach/orest-vue-demi-vue2` name and the vue-demi surface further mimic a legitimate ecosystem package the installer might expect to be safe.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
